b17b9d|obfuscation.text:
Bullying is a widespread problem among young people, and it has many causes. Poor parenting and low self-esteem are two of them, but in American schools racism is one of the most important reasons that Black students are mistreated. People often assume that this behavior fades as a person grows up. The events in Ferguson in 2014 suggest otherwise: the officer, in effect the bully, was not held to account. Just as schools and families can step in to stop bullying, political institutions can address mistreatment, and interest groups and parties can press the matter through a range of methods.

Demonstrators were angry about the grand jury's decision not to indict Darren Wilson. The government should let them use the rights given by the First Amendment, namely free speech and peaceful assembly, and the right to petition for a redress of grievances. If courts apply the clear and present danger test, protesters will see where the line lies between legitimate protest and damaging property or stopping people from getting to work. Protesters who stay within that line are more likely to be heard than those who cause disruption, as the Rodney King riots showed, where the damage did more harm than good for the cause. Courts should also treat Ferguson as a question of constitutional law, one that concerns civil rights and civil liberties. If the case is understood that way, the public may see the killing as a matter of civil mistreatment and not as an act of self-defense, and protests over the trial's outcome might become less frequent. The administration could also gather public opinion with probability sampling, so that each person has an equal chance of being picked, and publish the findings on television and social media. Protesters would then feel less pressure to stage dramatic acts that portray their communities badly.

Interest groups can strongly influence political institutions to take up their policies. A civil rights group with no economic aim, such as the NAACP, would be central here, since its stated mission is to end racial hatred and discrimination. It could rally supporters who share its views and lobby public officials, especially in the judiciary, to look at the case again. Such groups can also educate the public so that more people support their position. With solid research on the case and real commitment, the case might be reopened and the police killing might not go unpunished. The group would also build its credibility and be seen as a valuable voice on police brutality.

b17b9d|imitation.text:
Bullying is a sickness in the young and there are many reasons given for it. Bad raising and a low opinion of oneself and the other dark workings of the mind that leave a child wanting. These are some of them. But the first of them is race. It is why the black children are used so poorly in the schools. People say it passes when the child grows. It does not pass. In Ferguson in the year 2014 the bully was a policeman and the bully won.

The schools could put a stop to it and the parents could and so could the government of the country if it would. And the interest groups and the parties could come in and press the matter by whatever means they have.

The people were angry over the verdict that cleared Darren Wilson. They were angry and they had the right to be. The government must let them stand on what the Constitution gives them. The First Amendment. Free speech and the right to gather in peace and to ask the government to set right what is wrong. If the courts hold to the test of clear and present danger the people will learn where the line is between a protest and a riot. They will learn not to break the windows of other men's shops nor keep other men from their work. And when they stand within the line they will be heard. They will not be seen as the rioters of Rodney King who did more harm than they did good for their cause. The courts must look at Ferguson in the light of the law of the Constitution and the rights and liberties of the citizen. If they will do that then the people will see that a man was killed from mistreatment and not from self-defense and the protests that go on saying the trial was racist will in time grow fewer. The administration might ask the people what they think. A fair sample so that every person has the same chance of being asked. Then put the poll on the television and on the social media so that the protestors would not feel they must do some stunt in the streets of their own towns that shows them in a bad light.

The interest groups have a great hand in moving the government. The NAACP has no money in it. It has a mission and the mission is to end hatred of race and wrong done on account of race. It could call to it the ones who agree and go to the officials of the courts and ask them to look again at what was done. It could teach the public and win them to its side. With careful research into the case and the will to see it through the case might be opened again and the killing by the police might not go unpunished. And the group would earn the trust of men and be thought worth listening to on the matter of the police and their brutality.

b17b9d|simplification.text:
Bullying is a big problem for young people. There are many reasons for it. Some parents are not good. Some children do not feel good about themselves. But racism is a main reason that black students are treated badly in schools. Many people think bullying stops when a person gets older. The Ferguson case in 2014 shows this is not true. The police officer was like a bully. He won.

Schools can stop bullying. Parents can stop it. The government can stop mistreatment, too. Interest groups and political parties can also help. They can use many ways to bring attention to the problem.

Many people were angry about the court decision on Darren Wilson. The government should let these people use their rights. The First Amendment gives them the right to speak freely. It gives them the right to meet in peace. It gives them the right to ask the government to fix problems. Courts can use the clear and present danger test. Then protesters will know what they can and cannot do. They should not damage property. They should not stop people from going to work. Protesters who stay peaceful will get more attention. The Rodney King riots show the other side. There was a lot of damage, and the cause was hurt. The courts should look at Ferguson as a question of civil rights. Then people may understand that the killing was mistreatment. It was not self-defense. Fewer people may protest that the trial was racist. The government can also ask citizens what they think. It can choose people by chance, so everyone has an equal chance to be picked. Then it can show the results on television and social media. Protesters would not need to do dangerous acts in their towns. Those acts make them look bad.

Interest groups can help leaders change policy. The NAACP is a group for civil rights. Its main goal is to end racial hate and unfair treatment. It can ask people who agree with it to join. It can talk to public officials, especially in the courts. It can ask them to look at the case again. It can also teach the public so more people will support it. With good research and hard work, the case may open again. The police officer may not go free. The group will also gain trust. People will see it as an important voice on police violence.

b17b9d|backtranslation.text:
Bullying is a serious problem among the youth, and there are many explanations why it occurs. Poor parenting, low self-esteem and various other psychological processes that cause a deficit in the thinking of children may be examples, but racism is a main example of why African American students are treated badly in the school system. This attitude and the use of discrimination stem from an act that is supposed to end when the person grows up, yet in the Ferguson case in 2014 it seems the bully, the officer, won once more. As with school institutions, the American political institution can use its system to prevent such mistreatment, and as with parents, interest groups and parties can become involved and use different tactics to bring up the matter.

To respond to the demonstrators, who are angry about the controversial decision not to indict Darren Wilson, the American institution must allow them to exercise their rights under the Constitution, in particular the First Amendment of the Bill of Rights. It says that citizens have the right to "free speech" and "peaceful assembly" in order to petition the "government for a redress" of federal issues. If the clear and present danger test is applied to prevent "criminalized expression", the demonstrators will understand how to protest, instead of illegally damaging property and allegedly keeping people from their jobs. The demonstrators would then get more attention for their concern, rather than negative attention for disturbing the peace, unlike the demonstrators in the Rodney King riots, who caused more damage than they gave reasons for their cause. The judicial system should apply constitutional law more strongly to Ferguson, where the court "questions concerning civil rights and civil liberties". If the institution views the case in this way, demonstrators and even society will recognize and understand that the killing arose from civil mistreatment and was not excused as self-defense, which reduces protests that continue to claim the trial was the result of racism. The administration should also collect public opinion through probability sampling in order to "ensure that every person has an equal chance of being selected". It could then broadcast the poll on television and social media to publicize the opinions of American citizens, so that protesters would not feel compelled to perform certain stunts in their communities that could put them in a negative light.

Interest groups can play a very influential role in encouraging the political institution to promote their policies and ideas. The noneconomic civil rights interest group would play a main role in raising its concerns about the death of Mike Brown. In particular the NAACP, whose "principal mission is to eliminate racial hatred and racial discrimination". It could encourage members and individuals who agree with its statements, and lobby public officials directly, especially in the judicial branch, to reconsider the case. In connection with Ferguson, interest groups can also use education methods to "persuade the public to support their position". With high-quality research on the case and a commitment to support it, the case may be reopened and the perceived police crime may not go unpunished. The group will also build credibility and be regarded more as an asset in its view on police brutality.
